stories.headline: Cerebras Q2 revenue up 74% to $180M, backlog hits $25.4B, but shares fall 14%

key_facts.fact: Cerebras reported Q2 2026 GAAP revenue of $180.1 million, up 74% year over year, below the $194.23 million analysts expected.
key_facts.excerpt: Second-quarter sales rose 74.3 per cent to $180.11 million, while analysts expected $194.23 million, according to data compiled by LSEG.

key_facts.fact: Core revenue, which includes pass-through revenue, more than doubled to $209.9 million, and cloud and other services revenue jumped 281% to $126.0 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Record GAAP cloud and other services revenue of $126.0 million, up 281% year-over-year... GAAP total revenue of $180.1 million, up 74% year-over-year; Core total revenue of $209.9 million, up 103% year-over-year.

key_facts.fact: The company raised full-year 2026 core revenue guidance to $880-$890 million from $855-$865 million and said it plans to more than triple revenue in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Full Year 2026 Financial Outlook ... Core revenue of $880 to $890 million ... plan to more than triple revenue in 2027.

key_facts.fact: Remaining performance obligations totaled $25.4 billion as of June 30, a large share tied to the master relationship agreement with OpenAI, which committed to 750MW of capacity plus a $1.0 billion working-capital loan.
key_facts.excerpt: Remaining performance obligations totaled $25.4 billion, heavily concentrated in the OpenAI agreement... a secured promissory note of approximately $1.0 billion (the 'Working Capital Loan') funded by OpenAI in January 2026.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras posted a quarterly net loss of $450.5 million, driven by $377.0 million of stock-based compensation tied to its May IPO, which raised about $6.2 billion net.
key_facts.excerpt: the company posted a quarterly net loss of $450.5 million... largely due to sharply higher operating expenses and $377.0 million of quarterly stock-based compensation, much of it triggered by the IPO

key_facts.fact: The stock fell about 14-16% in extended trading despite the raised outlook; the company said it is not facing supply shortages as severe as other chip designers.
key_facts.excerpt: Still, Cerebras raised its annual revenue and gross margin forecasts and said it was not experiencing supply shortages as severe as other chip designers.

stories.headline: Cisco books $4B in hyperscaler AI orders in Q4, guides AI revenue to $7.5B in FY2027

key_facts.fact: Cisco took $4 billion of AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers in Q4 FY2026, bringing the fiscal-year total to $9.3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Significant momentum and raised expectations for AI infrastructure from hyperscalers - $4 billion of orders taken in Q4, bringing the total for FY 2026 to $9.3 billion

key_facts.fact: Total Q4 product orders rose 35% year over year (25% excluding hyperscalers), and networking product orders grew 40%, an eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth.
key_facts.excerpt: Q4 total product orders up 35% year over year; up 25% excluding hyperscalers... Networking product orders grew 40% year over year in Q4, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth

key_facts.fact: Q4 revenue was $17.3 billion, up 18%, and full-year FY2026 revenue a record $63.3 billion, up 12%; non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 rose 23%.
key_facts.excerpt: Record fiscal 2026 revenue of $63.3 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with Q4 revenue of $17.3 billion, up 18%... Non-GAAP EPS growth of 23% in Q4

key_facts.fact: Management guided AI infrastructure revenue to $7.5 billion in FY2027, up from about $3.8 billion in FY2026, when AI made up roughly 6% of total revenue versus under 2% in FY2025.
key_facts.excerpt: AI infrastructure revenue projected to grow to $7.5 billion in fiscal year 2027... in FY 2026, approximately 6% of our total revenue was from AI infrastructure for hyperscalers, up from less than 2% in FY 2025

key_facts.fact: Four of the top hyperscalers each grew AI infrastructure orders in triple digits; the mix was roughly 60% Silicon One systems and 40% optics, with Acacia optics alone topping $1 billion in Q4 orders.
key_facts.excerpt: four of the top hyperscalers each growing AI infrastructure orders in the triple digits... The mix of these orders in both Q4 and FY 2026 was approximately 60% Silicon One-based systems and 40% optics. Our Acacia business had another very strong quarter with over $1 billion in orders in Q4

key_facts.fact: Cisco also took over $400 million in AI infrastructure orders from neocloud, sovereign and enterprise customers in Q4, over $1 billion for the year, and guided FY2027 revenue to $72.2-$73.4 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Cisco guided FY2027 full-year revenue to $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion, and AI infrastructure revenue alone is expected to reach $7.5 billion in FY2027

stories.headline: SMIC profit triples to $479M as Chinese foundries ride an AI-driven chip shortage

key_facts.fact: SMIC's Q2 2026 net profit more than tripled to $479.2 million, far above the $283.1 million analysts expected, while revenue rose 36% year over year to $3.01 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's net profit more than tripled in the second quarter to $479.2 million, beating the $283.1 million expected by analysts in a Visible Alpha poll. Revenue rose 36% from a year earlier to $3.01 billion

key_facts.fact: SMIC net profit rose 261.7% year over year, while smaller rival Hua Hong's profit jumped 385.9% to $38.6 million on record revenue of $717.5 million, up 26.8%.
key_facts.excerpt: Net profits for SMIC and Hua Hong jumped 261.7 per cent and 385.9 per cent year on year to US$479.2 million and US$38.6 million, respectively... revenue at its smaller rival Hua Hong reached a record US$717.5 million in the quarter, up 26.8 per cent

key_facts.fact: Global foundries prioritizing AI capacity have created a severe shortage for non-AI chips, pushing international and domestic customers to shift mature-node orders to Chinese fabs.
key_facts.excerpt: non-AI sectors are dealing with a severe semiconductor shortage as global foundries increasingly prioritize capacity for AI-related demand. That has prompted many international and domestic clients to shift mature-node manufacturing orders to China

key_facts.fact: SMIC guided Q3 gross margin to 26%-28% and revenue up 2%-4% sequentially, signaling that price increases are outrunning cost pressure.
key_facts.excerpt: The company on Thursday forecast a further improvement in gross margin to between 26% and 28% in the third quarter, and said it expects quarterly revenue to rise 2%-4% sequentially

key_facts.fact: In a Thursday filing to the Hong Kong exchange, SMIC said AI spillover demand will persist in the second half and that it will accelerate new capacity to ease supply constraints.
key_facts.excerpt: "Looking ahead to the second half of this year, the industrial momentum and spillover effects generated by AI will persist, driving broad-based demand for integrated circuit manufacturing," SMIC said in a filing to the Hong Kong stock exchange on Thursday

stories.headline: Lenovo posts record $26.9B quarter, up 43%, as AI revenue jumps 60% to $9.3B

key_facts.fact: Lenovo reported record quarterly revenue of $26.94 billion for the quarter ended June 30, up 43% year over year, its fastest growth in five years.
key_facts.excerpt: overall Group revenue reached an all-time quarterly high of US$26.9 billion, up 43% year-on-year, with all business groups delivering record first-fiscal-quarter revenue and operating profit

key_facts.fact: AI-related revenue grew 60% year over year to $9.3 billion, or 35% of group revenue; adjusted net income rose 176% to $1.075 billion, above $1 billion for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: Adjusted net income was up 176% year-on-year to US$1.1 billion, surpassing the US$1 billion milestone for the first time ever... AI-related revenue grew 60% year-on-year to US$9.3 billion, accounting for 35% of total Group revenue in Q1.

key_facts.fact: Revenue beat the analyst consensus of $22.33 billion, but unadjusted results swung to a $609 million net loss on a non-recurring fair-value loss from revaluing warrants.
key_facts.excerpt: revenue in the three months ended June rose grew 43%... at $26.94 billion, beating market expectations for $22.33 billion... unadjusted net profit was hit by a nonrecurring fair-value loss due to the revaluation of its warrants and swung to a loss of $609 million

key_facts.fact: Revenue at the Infrastructure Solutions Group almost doubled on AI server demand, producing $777 million in operating profit, while the devices unit grew 27% despite surging memory costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue for this segment almost doubled, producing an operating profit of $777 million... Lenovo's intelligent-devices group, which includes PCs, smartphones and tablets, saw 27% revenue growth amid surging memory costs.

key_facts.fact: Worldwide PC shipments fell 4.9% year over year in April-June, the first decline after nine straight quarters of growth, as the memory shortage lifted device prices; Lenovo still led with 24.2% share.
key_facts.excerpt: Worldwide PC shipments fell 4.9% from a year earlier in the April-June period--the first decline after nine consecutive quarters of growth--as the memory shortage pushed up prices of consumer electronics, according to data from industry tracker IDC. Lenovo remained the world's leading PC maker... with a market share of 24.2%.

stories.headline: Memory maker CXMT passes Tencent as the most valuable Chinese company at $524B

key_facts.fact: On Thursday, CXMT surpassed Tencent by market capitalization to become the most valuable company listed on the mainland or in Hong Kong.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese memory chip maker CXMT on Thursday surpassed Tencent Holdings by market capitalization, becoming the most valuable company listed on the mainland or in Hong Kong.

key_facts.fact: CXMT's shares slipped 1.2% on Thursday but its market value stood at $524 billion, above Tencent's $510 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT, which debuted in Shanghai last month and quickly became China's largest onshore-listed company, fell 1.2% Thursday, leaving its market capitalization at $524 billion. Even so, it became more valuable than Tencent, whose valuation slid to $510 billion

key_facts.fact: Tencent's Hong Kong shares fell 4.5% on Thursday and are down more than 26% this year amid concerns over its rising AI investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite owning WeChat and game developer Riot Games, Tencent has struggled with its shares down over 26% this year... the move led to a 4.5% fall in its Hong Kong-listed stock on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: CXMT raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) in its July IPO and closed its first trading day up 465.82% from the 8.66-yuan offer price.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) in its initial public offering and its shares closed their first trading day at 49 yuan, up 465.82% from the 8.66-yuan IPO price.

key_facts.fact: Investors read the swap as a rotation toward AI hardware: 'CXMT exceeding Tencent is a message from the market, chips are the new clicks,' said Allspring portfolio manager Gary Tan.
key_facts.excerpt: Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, said, "CXMT exceeding Tencent is a message from the market, chips are the new clicks."

stories.headline: AI servers swallow 48% of all NAND shipped as China's YMTC breaks into the top three

key_facts.fact: Enterprise SSDs took 48% of global NAND bit shipments in Q2 2026, nearly double the 26% share a year earlier, as AI workloads shifted from training to inference.
key_facts.excerpt: AI inference workloads drove enterprise SSDs to 48% of global NAND shipments in Q2 2026, nearly double the 26% share a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: The resulting supply squeeze pushed NAND industry revenue to a record, rising fivefold from Q2 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The resulting supply tightness pushed industry revenue to record levels, rising fivefold from Q2 2025.

key_facts.fact: Samsung led shipments with 25%, down from 32% in Q2 2024 as it steered capacity to higher-margin DRAM; SK hynix was second at 22% after a 40% quarter-over-quarter jump in Solidigm bit shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung led shipments with 25%, down from 32% in Q2 2024 as it prioritized high-margin DRAM. SK hynix held second at 22% on a 40% QoQ jump in Solidigm bit shipments.

key_facts.fact: China's YMTC entered the global top three for the first time with a 14% shipment share, edging out Kioxia, but ranks only fifth by revenue because it sells mostly cheap consumer bits.
key_facts.excerpt: YMTC shipped 14% of the world's NAND flash in the second quarter of 2026, entering the global top three for the first time and narrowly displacing Kioxia... In terms of revenue, however, YMTC sits fifth behind both Kioxia and Micron, with nearly all of its output going into consumer products.

key_facts.fact: YMTC has been on the US Entity List since December 2022, which blocks Western server qualification and confines it largely to China's domestic and consumer channels.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has been included on the U.S. Entity List since December 2022, which bars it from achieving Western server qualification, where the big bucks are earned

key_facts.fact: Counterpoint expects server eSSDs to pass half of all NAND shipments by the end of 2026; YMTC's shipments rose 22% year over year and 5% quarter over quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: YMTC's shipments rose by 22% year-on-year and 5% quarter-on-quarter... Counterpoint Research analyzed, "By the end of this year, server eSSDs will account for more than half of all NAND shipments"

stories.headline: Seoul scraps permitting rules to unlock 4.2 trillion won in chip, AI data center and robot projects

key_facts.fact: South Korea on Thursday unveiled a deregulation package clearing land and construction rules that were holding up more than 4.2 trillion won of planned investment in semiconductors, batteries, biotech, AI data centers and robots.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea has hit the accelerator on President Lee Jae Myung's 'chip-and-beyond' industrial drive, clearing land and construction rules holding up more than 4.2 trillion won in planned investment

key_facts.fact: The biggest beneficiary is the Yongin semiconductor cluster: scrapping the 'one site, one permit' rule for large industrial complexes is expected to pull forward about 2.5 trillion won of investment.
key_facts.excerpt: It estimates the change can bring forward about 2.5 trillion won of investment at the Yongin cluster.

key_facts.fact: Gas-safety inspections for fab expansions will be shortened from seven days to three; fabs carry out roughly 1,800 such expansions a year.
key_facts.excerpt: Safety inspections required when semiconductor fabs expand their city-gas systems will also be shortened from seven days to three. The government said fabs can carry out roughly 1,800 such expansions a year

key_facts.fact: AI data centers get their own relief: server-room space will be excluded from some parking, elevator and artwork requirements, and clearer safety rules for collaborative and mobile industrial robots are due in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: server-room space will be excluded when calculating some parking, elevator and artwork-installation requirements under implementing rules for the AI Data Center Special Act. The government will also draw clearer safety rules for collaborative and mobile industrial robots

key_facts.fact: SK hynix plans four fabs at Yongin with the first cleanroom due in February 2027 and production as early as May, and has pulled completion of all four forward to 2033; Samsung targets its first Yongin fab in 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix plans four fabs there, with the first cleanroom due to open in February next year and production expected as early as May. Its target for completing all four fabs has been pulled forward to 2033. Samsung Electronics, which plans six fabs at its separate Yongin complex, is targeting completion of its first fab in 2029
